text:
incident-bot: Paging: SRE on-call (rotation: infra-rotation). Alert: service=/v1/stream p99 latency 3.2s > SLO(1.5s) and streaming stall rate increased to 6%. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.example/alerts/1790154321 :rotating_light:
oncall-sre: saw it, joining. grabbing logs and the initial runbook
adele: i'm on the metrics page — p95 jumped 600ms but p99 is the killer. tail latency spikes line up with spikes in cross-zone egress errors
kai: which path? region-azb->azc or cross-region?
oncall-sre: looks like inter-AZ egress to NAT gw in azc. traceroute from serving nodes shows extra 100ms hop after nat-azc-1
net-eng: could be NAT saturation or a routing flap. any packetloss on graphs?
oncall-sre: yes, packet loss metric at 0.8% from azb hosts to nat-azc-1 starting ~1790154000. TLS handshake latencies also spike for the same clients
leo: streaming stalls usually correlate with TLS renegotiation + retransmits. if NAT is dropping/queuing, connection stalls + p99 blow up
infra-rotation: I'm going to pull tcpdump from a representative host and the nat interface now. running:
```
ssh svc-edge@azb-host-17 "sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/azb-179015.pcap 'host 10.12.45.76'"
```
net-eng: also run `mtr` to the NAT IP and to public endpoint to see route AS path changes
oncall-sre: good call. starting mtr now.
customer-sre: FYI we've seen customer reports about degraded streaming in EU-west customers, flagged by support ticket #INC-7821
oncall-sre: handing update to @adele for mitigation while I dig deeper
adele: thanks. mitigation plan: 1) fail traffic for a subset of AZB -> NAT-AZC onto secondary NAT in AZB (local egress) 2) enable bypass route to avoid the suspected NAT node 3) throttle connections to force new TLS sessions through healthy path. executing step 1 for 10% of traffic via our routing control
kai: how are you toggling weights? use route-manager API?
adele: yes, route-manager PATCH to /v1/routes/egress with body:
```
{"route": "egress-azb", "overrides": [{"match": "svc-edge.azb", "weight": 10, "target": "nat-azb-2"}]}
```
adele: pushing now...
incident-bot: Deploy bot: route-manager change applied by adele at 1790154523 :white_check_mark:
adele: verified 10% traffic now egressing nat-azb-2. watching latency.
leo: can you capture tcp retransmit counts post-failover? that'll show if path cleared
oncall-sre: retran rate dropped to 0.1% on the sampled hosts that moved to nat-azb-2, p99 for that cohort down to 1.1s
net-eng: confirming, the nat-azc-1 metrics show CPU and conntrack table rising around the time of spike. looks like conntrack exhaustion causing drop/queue
infra-rotation: grabbing conntrack stats:
```
sudo conntrack -S | grep entries
# output: entries=1999800 limit=2000000
```
infra-rotation: we were hitting the conntrack limit on nat-azc-1, causing drops.
kai: can we safely increase conntrack limit and restart conntrack on nat-azc-1? risk: short term, needs conntrack module reload which may drop sessions. prefer draining and failover
adele: agree. we'll scale up nat-azc-1 (add a sibling nat instance) and shift weights away from it, then remove target once healthy. starting immediate scaling action with autoscale API.
incident-bot: Autoscaler: requested 1 additional nat-azc instance (order #asm-879). ETA ~2m
customer-sre: letting support know we're doing targeted failovers. asking for affected customer list for proactive updates
noncall-sre: quick note: streaming stall metric across the fleet peaked then began tailing down after first 10% shift. looks like partial mitigation worked. need full mitigation for all traffic.
adele: plan step 2: shift 70% traffic to nat-azb-2 and 30% to new nat-azc-2 when it comes up. doing incremental change to avoid overwhelming nat-azb-2
net-eng: also rotate iptables conntrack timeout for ESTABLISHED to reduce state size while new instances stabilize (short-term knob).
leo: watch TLS handshake rate too. If we force new sessions we might cause handshake spiky loads. throttling open sockets per-second is safer
infra-rotation: new nat instance is up: nat-azc-2 registered and healthy according to healthcheck at 1790154899
incident-bot: Autoscaler: nat-azc-2 healthy and registered
adele: shifting weights now: patching to 70% nat-azb-2 and 30% nat-azc-2 for azb egress
adele: change applied. monitoring...
oncall-sre: p99 down fleet-wide to 1.4s and streaming stalls down to 1.2%. still above SLO but headed in right direction
kai: net-eng manually cleared conntrack entries on nat-azc-1 to relieve pressure while we fail traffic away: `conntrack -F` executed at 1790155020
net-eng: note: we saw TTL reduction on azc router to nat-azc-1 at 1790153980 which aligns with a BGP flap to that device. vendor confirms transient control plane issue in azc switch fabric
leo: root cause likely conntrack exhaustion exacerbated by transient routing flap causing retransmits and TLS handshake spikes.
oncall-sre: good candidate RCA. for post-incident actions: 1) increase conntrack limit on nat instances 2) add alerting on conntrack usage and error counts 3) create runbook for graceful conntrack drain and failover 4) vendor follow-up on switch fabric BGP instability
customer-sre: i'll prepare customer-visible incident summary and send proactive messages to impacted accounts.
adele: will keep the thread open until all traffic normalized and we finish handoff to infra-rotation for postmortem.
infra-rotation: taking handoff. final status at 1790157620: p99 stabilized at 0.9s, streaming stalls back to baseline 0.2%, nat-azc-1 retired for investigation, nat-azc-2 handling steady load.
oncall-sre: thanks all. logging timeline and saving pcaps at /var/incidents/1790154321/ for PM.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-1790154321. Severity: Sev2. Current owners: infra-rotation, net-eng.
adele: I'll start the postmortem draft and include actions above. tagging @kai for network diagram updates. :thumbsup:
